title: Choose CueBench's visual world
question: Which operating world should CueBench carry into its evidence-led caption and audio-description workbench?

options.label: Projection Proof
options.lineage: annotated classroom transparencies and shared teaching slides
options.thesis: The video is the shared sheet; agents add transparent timed marks and the teacher settles the record.
options.viewport: A luminous video-and-timeline evidence field owns two thirds of the desktop while a numbered review docket anchors the right and the Court Record rests in a lower drawer.
options.risk: Transparency becomes visual noise unless only the selected evidence layer lifts above the sheet.

raised.raise: Status banks use unmistakable label, shape, and color changes instead of delicate tint shifts.
Finding focus traces a brief visible path from validation result to its exact moment on the timeline.
The selected evidence plane holds completely still while surrounding layers visibly recede.

options.label: Calibration Bench
options.lineage: classroom science instruments and oscilloscope calibration
options.thesis: Caption timing becomes a measured signal that a teacher and agent calibrate against visible evidence.
options.viewport: A large specimen bay holds the video, a calibrated signal rail spans beneath it, and the docket reads like precise bench measurements without hiding full caption text.
options.risk: Its familiar professional-tool grammar may feel too technical for a teacher's first captioning session.

options.label: Hard-Plane Review
options.lineage: Precisionist industrial plates and operator control surfaces
options.thesis: Video, timeline, findings, and docket become interlocking planes; the active plane alone takes the light.
options.viewport: The video plane dominates left, the timeline overlaps its lower edge, and a slate docket plane on the right reveals selected evidence through strict geometry.
options.case: It matches CueBench's structural clarity but identifies with industrial operators more than teachers.
options.risk: Stencil typography and hard mass can make careful accessibility review feel severe.

options.label: Revision Sheet
options.lineage: one-sheet fold sequences and recoverable crease diagrams
options.thesis: Every immutable cue revision remains a visible crease in one continuous timed sheet.
options.viewport: The selected video and cue sit on one large working sheet while revision lineage runs as deliberate steps beneath and the review docket forms a narrow margin.
options.case: It makes revision history unusually legible, but the paper ritual is less native to timed media than the assigned world.
options.risk: Cultural specificity and soft paper texture can distract from evidence accuracy if treated decoratively.

options.label: Time Signal
options.lineage: seven-segment clocks, scoreboards, and timing instruments
options.thesis: Time, readiness, and validation illuminate in fixed slots while full caption language remains calm and readable.
options.viewport: Large time and validation masks lock the upper rail, with video and waveform beneath and readable caption prose in a separate docket plane.
options.case: It makes time and state immediate, but its native alphabet cannot carry the transcript without breaking its own system.
options.risk: The dark luminous register can resemble the generic neon AI dashboard CueBench explicitly rejects.

options.label: Elbow Panel
options.thesis: Workflow states travel through thick color-banked routes around the workbench.
options.viewport: A sweeping elbow frame routes video, timeline, and docket through ranked pill segments.
options.case: The active-state grammar is excellent, but teachers do not identify with a fictional console and the frame competes with evidence.

options.label: Gravity Garden
options.lineage: directional rain fields and causal paths
options.thesis: Findings visibly flow toward the exact cue, gap, or evidence that caused them.
options.viewport: A timeline field bends findings toward cues while video and docket sit as quiet anchors.
options.case: Cause and effect is memorable, but the garden metaphor weakens task recognition and predictable editing controls.
options.risk: Animation would obscure rather than clarify routine review.

options.label: Depth Queue
options.lineage: bitmap scrollers and ranked depth planes
options.thesis: Brightness, spacing, and motion depth rank every unresolved piece of work without enclosing it.
options.viewport: The selected cue holds still at the front while findings, timeline, and record occupy receding baseline planes.
options.case: Focus hierarchy is strong, but removing enclosure and dividers damages scanning, accessibility, and teacher familiarity.
options.kept: Complete stillness at the focus plane.
options.risk: Sparse darkness hides the relationship among video, cue, evidence, and ruling.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark professional video editor with familiar panels, a blue playhead, and conventional caption cards.
canonCard.viewport: Video and waveform fill the left, a dense caption inspector fills the right, and export controls sit in a top toolbar.
canonCard.risk: Immediately understandable but indistinguishable from existing editors and intimidating to occasional teachers.
